idiom_name: class Adapter(private val adaptee: Adaptee) : Target by adaptee, with overrides for translated members
implementation_notes: Kotlin supports delegation in the language: `class Adapter(private val adaptee: Adaptee) : Target by adaptee` makes the compiler generate every Target member that forwards to the adaptee with zero boilerplate, and any member whose signature or meaning differs is written as an override - noting that overridden members are invisible to the delegate's own methods, which can only see its own implementations. Where the adaptee does not implement Target at all, that mismatch is still written by hand. Extension functions cover the other half of the problem: they add target-shaped operations to a type you cannot modify without any wrapper object, at the cost of being resolved statically and being invisible to code that does not import them.
pitfalls: `by` only forwards members of the interface the delegate actually implements: a missing member is a compile error, and an override written in the adapter is never seen by the delegate's own methods.
Extension functions are resolved statically: a member function of the same name always wins, and two extensions with the same signature in different files silently shadow each other.
Extensions cannot reach private members and are not virtual; if the translation needs the adaptee's internals or must be overridable, write the wrapper class.
Do not widen the declared Target interface just to make `by` compile - that publishes members the client should never see.

variants.name: Adapter methods as extension functions
variants.implementation_notes: When the caller only needs 'the adaptee should also be usable as X', extension functions add the target operations to the adaptee's type directly: no wrapper object, no delegation chain, no class to keep in sync, and the call site reads as a member (legacyUser.toUser()). Kotlin's own standard library adapts types this way, for example StringBuilder.appendLine(). Prefer extensions for stateless additive translation on types you cannot modify; prefer the wrapper class when the translation is stateful, must be discoverable as a type, or would otherwise scatter across modules.
variants.idiom_name: fun LegacyUser.toUser(): User extension on the adaptee type
variants.code_sketch:
fun LegacyUser.toUser(): User =
    User(fullName = "$firstName $lastName", email = emailAddress)

val users = legacyUsers.map(LegacyUser::toUser)   // reads as a member
pitfalls: Static resolution: a member function of the same name silently wins over the extension, so an upstream API addition can change behaviour without a compiler error.
Scattered extensions make it hard to see which type gained which capability - keep adapter extensions in the adapter's file or module.
An extension that needs state must capture it, which turns the extension back into a hidden wrapper.
